title: Service Continuity: Pausing and Resuming the Workplace Cafe Management Program
content:
A client holding a Workplace Cafe Management Program contract may pause counter service without ending the contract, for a building closure, a floor move or a seasonal shutdown.

**When a pause may be taken.** A pause is only taken on a contract that stands active or suspended — read from the contract's own status on record, taken before the pause is recorded, for that contract alone. A pause shorter than the minimum suspension printed against the service model is handled as ordinary closed days rather than as a suspension: hypothetically, a pause of 2 calendar days, shorter than a hypothetical minimum suspension of 5 calendar days for its service model, would be treated as ordinary closed days, while a pause of 5 calendar days, meeting that hypothetical minimum, would just qualify as a suspension in its own right.

For each month or part month of pause the standby charge was raised, calculated as the standby percentage printed against the service model applied to the monthly management fee, with the management fee itself not raised for the same period — that clause is **no longer in force** and has been superseded by the current basis for charging a paused contract.

Suspended days accumulate against the contract year ceiling printed against the service model; once the ceiling is reached the pause is not extended further, and the client is asked either to resume service or to give notice of termination.

Resumption needs the notice printed against the service model, counted in calendar days, and the resumption day is the first day the standby charge stops accruing.

Where the client asked to resume sooner than the resumption notice allowed, the cafe reopened on the earliest day the notice permitted and the standby charge ran to that day — that clause is likewise **no longer in force** and superseded by the current basis. No figure of the current basis is given here.

The standby percentage of the monthly management fee, the minimum suspension length, the contract year ceiling on suspended days, and the resumption notice remain those printed against the service model, and stay valid entries against each service model.
